purpose: Define how Ireland Housing Data monitors authoritative sources for changes that may affect legal propositions, procedures, evidence routes, deadlines or published answers.
core_principle: MONITOR SOURCE → DETECT CHANGE → CLASSIFY CHANGE → MAP DEPENDENCIES → REVERIFY ONLY WHAT IS AFFECTED
watch_targets: Irish Statute Book Acts and statutory provisions
official court judgments and legal sources
impact_rules: A source change does not automatically invalidate every answer using that source.
An amendment is not treated as operative until commencement and transitional rules are checked.
A new judgment affects only propositions within its actual legal scope.
A procedure-page change may affect route/access information without changing substantive law.
A source becoming unavailable is not evidence that the underlying legal or property fact disappeared.
Historical snapshots remain anchored to their applicable historical sources unless a material historical dependency changes.
priority_rules: P0_IMMEDIATE_REVIEW_REQUIRED for material current legal/deadline changes affecting published answers.
P1_HIGH_PRIORITY for material current property/procedure/route changes.
P2_STANDARD_REVIEW for ordinary material source changes.
P3_MONITOR for changes with no presently identified material dependency.
NO_REVIEW_REQUIRED where change is demonstrably outside all material dependencies.
hard_stops: Never silently rewrite a published answer because a source changed.
Never treat a changed webpage as proof of changed law without legal-source verification.
Never treat source disappearance as legal repeal or property-record deletion.
Never use freshness as a substitute for authority.
Never skip dependency analysis before mass invalidation.
